To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the enolate ions derived from cyclic β-keto-esters are nucleophilic and that their reactivities are similar to those of the enolate ions of acyclic β-keto ester anions, except for those derived from δ-lacotones, which are less reactive.

enolates derived from oxocarboxylic acid derivatives are less nucleophilically reactive than enolates derived form acyclic ketones, and that enolates from δ-lactone are even less reactive than enolats from oxocarbylic acid derivatives.

the nucleophilic reaction of an enolate ion with an electrophile can be described by a second-order rate law, first order in the electrophile, and first order in the enolate ion, and that the rate constant for the reaction of the enolate ion is influenced by the presence of an ion pair, which can be quantified by using the crown ether 18-crown6 and by using K+ as an ion pair partner.

the nucleophilicities of the enolate ions are determined by the steric properties of the ester molecules.

the reactivities of the anions of cyclic β-keto-esters, as measured by their reactions with benzhydryl cations, are not affected by the presence of a five- or six-membered ring in the ester moiety.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reactivities of enolate ions derived from acyclic, five-membered, and six-membered cyclic esters are similar, but that the reactivities decrease with the size of the ring.

the nucleophilic reactions of enolate ions derived from β-keto ester anions are not affected by ring strain, and that the nucleophilicity of the anions is not influenced by the conformation of the starting β-keto esteric acid.
the reactivities of the enolate ions are determined by the basicities of the enolate anions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nucleophilicities of the enolate ions derived from cyclic esters are similar to those derived from their acyclic counterparts.
the nucleophilicities of enolate ions derived from cyclic β-ketoesters are similar to those of acyclic β-ketoesters.
, in general, the nucleophilicity of enolate ions is not significantly affected by the ring size of the cyclic β-keto acid from which they are derived.
